Settings control room

Settings is now a searchable control room: icon rail, Booking vs Schedule, matching titles, related jumps, and stable save bars.

Side by side

Matched Cursor IDE Chromium captures at 1372×1160 CSS pixels (PNGs 2744×2320), ADMIN, dark appearance, authenticated local Preview at 127.0.0.1:3000. Parallel page-chrome work is also visible in the global sidebar (account at the bottom, Notifications no longer in the rail). Settings-specific change is the inner control room.

After only

The Profile baseline landed on the loading skeleton, so it is not a trustworthy loaded-form comparison. Sports, Checkout policies, Notifications, and overview filter had no matched before.

What changed, and why

Settings is a directory, not a dump of tabs

Was

Overview listed every page in mixed People / Inventory / Scheduling groups. Finding Kiosks or overdue meant scanning the rail.

Now

In-page filter plus Resume. Booking and Schedule are separate jobs. Sports sits with calendars and locations.

Each tab shares one shell

Was

Titles drifted from nav labels. Long pages had no jump. Related work lived in other groups with no cross-links.

Now

Titles come from SETTINGS_SECTIONS. Related links sit under every tab. Sports and Security get on-page jump nav.

Saves and empty states say what they mean

Was

Some forms swapped button labels while saving. Profile omitted Slack. Collaborator empty/dirty states were easy to misread.

Now

Shared save bars keep Saved / Save changes / Saving stable. Profile writes slackHandle. Empty and dirty states stay explicit.

Verification

  • Authenticated Preview as Erik Role ADMIN at http://127.0.0.1:3000. Overview filter, Profile loaded form, Appearance, Notifications, Sports jump nav, and Checkout policies dirty/reset save bar were exercised in the Cursor browser.
  • Focused source tests: tests/settings-ui-polish-source.test.ts, tests/settings-sweeping-ui-contract.test.ts, tests/breadcrumbs.test.ts.
  • npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false and npm run lint run after the review page.
  • npm run build:app was not run because Preview next dev already owns port 3000.

Things to know

  • Route URLs and role gates did not change. App activity remains owner-only and off the default rail.
  • Profile first paint is still slow enough that a snapshot can land on skeletons; wait for the form before judging the page.
  • The Settings directory filter and the global ⌘K palette are separate. A leftover palette from a prior shortcut can sit over the overview until Escape.
  • Parallel uncommitted page-chrome work is visible in these captures and was preserved.
